### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via os plugin publish (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bba7ff03d24bbb7edb7d83cf658c599d55d32463` — the merge of head `263039c193a9c9986fe2913e5f589af7ddecbba1` into base `2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bba7ff03d24bbb7edb7d83cf658c599d55d32463 && git checkout bba7ff03d24bbb7edb7d83cf658c599d55d32463
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783 263039c193a9c9986fe2913e5f589af7ddecbba1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783 && git merge --no-ff 263039c193a9c9986fe2913e5f589af7ddecbba1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2e955dde6c058e629a439714695667184f5cb783` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `263039c193a9c9986fe2913e5f589af7ddecbba1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts, packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts, packages/cli/test/plugin-publish-manifest-entry.test.ts, packages/cli/test/plugin-publish.test.ts + packages/runtime/src/index.ts (exports), packages/runtime/package.json (`exports`), packages/runtime/src/installed-plugin-loader.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/install.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts (`.changeset/27914-publish-decodes-manifest-once.md` is a prose face: the lane seat's ACCEPT)

Owed on the declaration face alone (`Clause-②: yes (widening)`); the diff touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path, so the tier is `TIER_DEFAULT`, written by the lane seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published surface.** `@objectstack/runtime` exports only `.`; `src/index.ts:75-76` re-exports `readCompiledPluginManifest` and the type `CompiledPluginManifestRead`. The `ok` arm gains `document: Record<string, unknown>`. That is a key added to a returned type reachable from the entry, so the declaration `yes (widening)` is right, and the claim's original `no` was amended to match (claim 6520509261).
- **Every existing key keeps its value.** `manifest` is still `ManifestSchema.safeParse(raw).data`; the `ok: false` arm is byte-identical; `unreadable` still covers a missing entry and a non-object document (pinned in the new runtime test).
- **`document` is the decoded entry, before the parse.** It is the same object handed to `safeParse`; zod does not mutate its input, so the defaults the parse stamps (`scope`, `defaultDatasource`) are absent from it (pinned: `read.manifest` has `scope`, `read.document` has neither).
- **Consumers.** The three in-repo readers (`installed-plugin-loader.ts:363`, `install.ts:302`, `osplugin.ts:153`) read `ok` / `manifest` / `reason` / `issues` only; none constructs the type or spreads the answer into a payload, so an extra key changes nothing they emit. Out-of-repo readers can only gain a key.
- **The upload stays verbatim.** `publish.ts` now uploads `read.document` instead of re-decoding the entry it found by `MANIFEST_FILENAME`. Same bytes decoded by the same `JSON.parse`, so the `plugin_manifest` payload is unchanged; the existing end-to-end test now also pins key order against the archive entry, and the new CLI test pins it with the CLI constant spelled differently from the runtime's (red on `main` at the second lookup's non-null `find`, per the thread's report).
- Wrong: none found.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset`: `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cli` `patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, line-initial; the PR body carries the same two lines and `Skills-docs: none` with its grep.
- `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3). No BREAKING banner is owed: nothing is removed or narrowed. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Out of scope, carded by the seat:** `publish.ts`'s integrity preflight still names its exempt list with the CLI's `MANIFEST_FILENAME`, and `build.ts` / `install.ts` spell the same file with that constant while the runtime reads `COMPILED_PLUGIN_MANIFEST_FILE`. The new CLI test sidesteps it on purpose (no `integrity` map). Not this card's rule (one decode, no second lookup), so not a blocker here.
- Check-runs at this head were still in progress when read (45: 16 success, 13 skipped, 16 running). Landing waits for all green.

### ④ Design judgment

- **`compiled-plugin-manifest.ts`:** answering the decoded document beside the parsed value is the right altitude: the one function that finds and decodes the entry is the one that hands it back, so a door that forwards the artifact's own manifest no longer needs to know the filename. The TSDoc on the arm says which to forward and why.
- **`publish.ts`:** the non-null `find` and second `JSON.parse` are gone; the comment states the invariant (the upload is the signed bytes' own manifest).
- **Tests:** the runtime pin covers the new key and the unchanged refusals; the CLI pin reproduces the filename drift the card names; the end-to-end control stays green.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8qhl4f`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia (lane seat)`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Seat ACCEPT · PR #28075 · head `263039c193a9c9986fe2913e5f589af7ddecbba1` · 2026-10-30T11:59Z

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** `os plugin publish` 读插件包里的编译清单只解析一次：`@objectstack/runtime` 的 `readCompiledPluginManifest` 在返回解析结果的同时，带回它解码出的原始清单 `document`，publish 直接上传它（#27914）。
- **为什么改：** 原来 publish 校验完又按 CLI 自己拼的文件名再找一次、再解析一次；两边常量一旦拼写不同就会在第二次查找处崩溃。
- **风险与回滚：** 上传内容逐字节不变（仍是包内原样清单，不带解析时补的默认值）；回滚即还原两个源文件。对外导出类型多了一个字段（加宽，非破坏）。
- **先看：** `packages/runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts` 的 `ok` 分支，和 `publish.ts` 里 `read.document` 那一行。
- **两分钟验证：** 对任一 `.osplugin` 跑 `os plugin publish`，云端收到的 `plugin_manifest` 与包内 `objectstack.plugin.json` 一致。
- **需要你做的：** 无（Tier S；契约复核已 PASS，按本期落地授权由席位落地）。

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** draft → main, `Fixes #27914`. 6 files (+137/−10): `runtime/src/compiled-plugin-manifest.ts` + new test, `cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts`, two CLI tests, one changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 28075`: NOT governed.
- **Premise:** re-measured by the thread; the filename-drift pin is red on `main` (TypeError at the second lookup) and green on this head; the byte-identical upload control is green on both.
- **Contract review:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body, the changeset and (amended) the claim; `TIER_DEFAULT` record by the lane seat, **PASS**, comment 6521886792, at this head. No new head since.
- **Declarations:** `Metadata-protocol: none`; `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/cli` `patch` (a non-protocol widening ships `patch`). `Skills-docs: none` with its grep.
- **Out of scope:** the CLI still spells the manifest filename with its own constant in publish's integrity exempt list, build and install → #28080 (p3, triage).
- **Gate check-runs on this head:** 48 total, 35 success, 13 skipped by the path filter, 0 failed. `mergeable_state: clean`.
- **Landing:** Tier S, under the maintainer's landing grant for this term (2026-10-29 22:05Z, seat thread). Ready + auto-merge through the relay.

**ACCEPT**
